fit: olive-oil-enriched diet and incretin response in normal rats
assessment: The early GLP-1 increment was higher, and glucose tolerance improved at day 36. Gut tissue GLP-1 content was comparable at day 50. The original congress report and paper are one family. Bowel motility and oil grade were unverified.

fit: olive-oil-enriched diet in a separate streptozotocin rat model
assessment: The rat cohort had greater acute GLP-1 release with oil but lower chronic weight gain, lower intestinal GLP-1 content and no improvement in oral glucose tolerance. The outcome and model do not answer the frozen symptom.

fit: olive oil within a supplied 28-day Mediterranean diet
assessment: In 22 men, systolic pressure was lower after the mixed diet. No ingredient-specific comparison or bowel, anxiety or insomnia outcome was reported.

fit: olive-oil comparator capsules for a fish-oil metabolic study
assessment: The olive-oil group was an active dietary comparator, with no oil-free arm and no matched symptom measure.

fit: pooled beverage use in a shift-work survey
assessment: A self-selected sample of 260 workers reported energy effects and 35% reported coffee or tea use for symptoms. Reported beverage use is pooled and there is no response comparison. A parallel conference report shares the same survey.

fit: afternoon coffee break with social contact in a group-home case
assessment: Requests for pain relief initially decreased during a combined activity and then recurred. The subsequent history linked pain to the menstrual cycle. No dose, independent coffee effect or measured fatigue outcome was recorded.

fit: reported heartburn after coffee in an iron-deficiency case
assessment: The case includes a coffee-triggered heartburn report and an explicit denial of fatigue. It gives no clinical effect estimate for coffee on Parkinson fatigue.

fit: caffeine pill history alongside other exposures and anabolic steroid use
assessment: Caffeine was a reported pre-exercise exposure. The case did not isolate it from other exposures or measure Parkinson fatigue.

fit: instant coffee versus water with arterial and ECG endpoints
assessment: The two abstracts report no arterial-wave or pressure difference and longer QTc after instant coffee at two points. They use overlapping protocols and may share participants. They give no brewed-coffee or fatigue result.

fit: filtered and unfiltered coffee in a coronary event case-control study
assessment: The authors observed different preparation associations in people with diabetes. A fatigue endpoint and directional test of the frozen exposure are absent.
